skill.name: spawn:terminal
skill.description: Open a separate terminal window for non-AI CLI commands after reviewing command help and selecting output capture settings.
skill.summary: Launch user-requested CLI commands in a separate terminal with optional output capture and logging.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: The prose-only backtick and fixed relative-path detections are false positives. Five instructions or examples confirm intentional external command execution, and checking help does not constrain dangerous command syntax. No prompt injection or separate semantic threat was found.

remediation.issue: User-selected commands can be launched without a command allowlist or explicit risk review.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation showing the executable and arguments before launching commands with destructive, privileged, or network effects.

remediation.issue: A help check does not prevent shell metacharacters, command substitution, or unsafe arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Pass executable names and arguments as structured values, reject shell control operators, and avoid shell interpretation by default.

content.user_title: Run CLI Commands in New Terminal Windows
content.value_statement: Long-running CLI commands can occupy the active session and hide progress. This skill opens a separate terminal after checking command help.
actual_capabilities: Identifies the non-AI CLI command requested by the user.
Runs the selected command with its help option before launch.
Launches command strings in a separate terminal through fork_terminal().
Supports blocking output capture for commands that must complete before returning.
Can write complete terminal output to a debug file.
limitations: Depends on a companion fork_terminal() implementation outside this skill directory.
Does not validate command safety beyond reviewing help output.
Handles non-AI CLI processes and redirects AI agent requests to another skill.
Opening a new terminal window depends on the host environment.

use_cases.title: Convert Media in a Separate Terminal
use_cases.description: Launch an ffmpeg conversion separately while preserving complete output in a debug file.

use_cases.title: Run Frontend Build Tasks
use_cases.description: Start an npm build in another terminal without occupying the active assistant session.

use_cases.title: Capture CLI Diagnostics
use_cases.description: Run a diagnostic command in blocking mode and return its captured output for review.

prompt_templates.title: Launch a Basic Command
prompt_templates.prompt: Open a new terminal and run [command]. Check its help first, then launch it without output capture.

prompt_templates.title: Save Terminal Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Run [command] in a new terminal. Review its help first and save the complete output to a debug file.

prompt_templates.title: Wait for Captured Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Start [command] in blocking capture mode after checking its help. Return the captured output and log file path.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Complex CLI Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this non-AI CLI task: [task]. Select a command, inspect help, explain important options, then launch it with requested capture settings.

output_examples.input: Open a new terminal and run the npm build without capture.
output_examples.output: Reviewed npm help and opened a separate terminal for the build. Output capture and file logging are disabled.

output_examples.input: Convert the video to a GIF and save complete terminal output.
output_examples.output: Reviewed ffmpeg help, launched the conversion in a new terminal, and returned the debug log path.

output_examples.input: Run the Python diagnostic and wait for its result.
output_examples.output: Reviewed Python help, completed the diagnostic in blocking mode, and returned the captured terminal output.

best_practices: Review the exact executable, arguments, files, and destinations before launch.
Enable file logging when command output is needed for later diagnosis.
Use blocking capture only when the next task depends on command completion.
anti_patterns: Do not launch destructive or privileged commands without explicit user confirmation.
Do not treat help output as proof that a command is safe.
Do not use this skill to start Claude, Codex, or another AI agent.

faq.question: What commands can this skill run?
faq.answer: It can launch non-AI CLI commands supported by the host environment through the companion terminal helper.

faq.question: Does it check command syntax?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow requires reviewing the selected command help before launching the full command.

faq.question: Can it return command output?
faq.answer: Yes. Blocking capture waits for completion and returns the command output.

faq.question: Can it save terminal output?
faq.answer: Yes. File logging can preserve complete terminal output and return the log path.

faq.question: Can it launch AI coding agents?
faq.answer: No. Requests for Claude, Codex, Gemini, and similar agents should use the separate agent skill.

faq.question: Does the skill guarantee command safety?
faq.answer: No. Help review checks syntax, but users must still assess permissions, side effects, and untrusted arguments.
